system.name: Design system
system.description: A token-driven design system in React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4, with light and dark themes. Every color, size, space and motion value comes from one JSON file, so changing a token changes every component that uses it.

facts.label: Themes
facts.text: Light (Warm Editorial) and dark (Dark Precision), switched with a data-theme attribute on the root element.

facts.label: Accessibility
facts.text: Built to WCAG 2.2 AA, with one documented exception (control borders).

facts.label: Tokens
facts.text: tokens/tokens.json is the single source of truth. Figma variables come from it through Token Sync.

components.name: Button

intro.text: Primary, secondary, ghost and danger variants; three sizes; loading and disabled states; optional leading and trailing icons.

whenToUse.text: Primary is for the one main action on a screen.
whenToUse.source: Button.tsx, comment on the variant prop

whenToUse.text: Secondary: a supporting action next to a primary button, such as Cancel.
Ghost: a low-emphasis action, such as one inside a toolbar or a table row.
Danger: an action that deletes something or cannot be undone.
Sizes: sm for dense tables and toolbars, md for default buttons, lg for primary mobile actions.
whenToUse.source: tokens/tokens.json, descriptions of primitive.size.control-sm, control-md and control-lg

states.name: default
states.text: The resting look of each variant.
states.source: Button.tsx, comment on the resting styles

states.name: hover
states.text: Hover feedback, only applied while the button is usable.
states.source: Button.tsx, comment on the feedback styles

states.name: pressed
states.text: Pressed feedback, only applied while the button is usable.
states.source: Button.tsx, comment on the feedback styles

states.name: focus
states.text: A visible 2px focus ring on keyboard focus.

states.name: disabled
states.text: Uses dedicated disabled colors, not opacity.

states.name: loading
states.text: Shows a spinner and ignores clicks. The button stays focusable and keeps its width.
states.source: Button.tsx, comment on the loading prop

accessibility.text: A visible 2px focus ring on keyboard focus for every interactive element, in both themes.
A button needs either visible text or an aria-label (icon-only buttons).
Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled, so the button stays focusable. Disabled uses the native disabled attribute.
accessibility.source: Button.tsx, attributes on the button element

accessibility.text: Interactive targets are at least 24px, and the small button gets a 44px hit area on mobile.
The loading spinner stops spinning when the user prefers reduced motion.
Leading and trailing icons are hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden).

knownGaps: Secondary pressed uses button/ghost/bg-pressed in code; there is no button/secondary/bg-pressed token. The Figma variant follows the code.
Ghost has no background token; its resting fill is plain transparent in code, so the Figma fill is empty.
The spinner stroke is 2 SVG units in code with no token. Figma binds it to border-width/emphasis, which is also 2px.
The 44px mobile hit area (button/target-touch) is invisible in code and is not drawn in Figma.
Not built in Figma: leadingIcon, trailingIcon and fullWidth.

The focus ring is a separate rectangle. Its size is the button size plus the ring offset, so that size is calculated from the variable values and is not bound. Its corner radius uses the button radius without the offset.
State names (hover, pressed, focus) are CSS states in code, not props.

components.name: Input

intro.text: Label, helper text, error, success, loading and disabled states.
intro.source: README.md, Components (read-only and required are left out of this Figma component)

whenToUse.text: Use for a single line of text, such as a name or an email address.
The label is always visible. Inputs are never labelled by placeholder alone.
whenToUse.source: Input.tsx, comment on the label prop

whenToUse.text: Use helper text for a format hint. Use the error message to say what to fix.
A required input adds "(required)" to its label.

states.name: default
states.text: The resting field. It shows the placeholder.

states.name: focus
states.text: The border grows from the default width to the emphasis width and changes to the focus color.
states.source: Input.tsx, comment above the field styles

states.name: error
states.text: The error message turns the field into its error state: emphasis border width, error border color and an error message with an icon.
states.source: Input.tsx, comment on the error prop

states.name: success
states.text: Shows the success message with a check icon.
states.source: Input.tsx, comment on the success prop

states.name: loading
states.text: Shows a spinner inside the field and sets aria-busy.
states.source: Input.tsx, comment on the loading prop

states.name: disabled
states.text: Uses dedicated disabled colors, not opacity.

accessibility.text: The label is tied to the field with htmlFor, and helper and message text are linked with aria-describedby.
An error sets aria-invalid and its message uses role="alert". A success message uses role="status".

The input border has a contrast of about 1.4:1, below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks for. This is a recorded decision. Each input has other cues: a visible label, a surface fill that differs from the page, and a focus ring checked at 3:1 or better.
A visible 2px focus ring on keyboard focus for every interactive element, in both themes.
The loading spinner stops spinning when the user prefers reduced motion.

knownGaps: The Figma component has a typed width of 320px. In code the input is as wide as its container and no width token exists. A token would need to be proposed first.
Read-only and filled are left out on purpose. README lists read-only but Input.tsx has no read-only styling or tokens.
The error and success icons are plain filled circles, not the glyphs in code.
In code the focus state changes the border only (no separate ring). The Figma variant follows the code. README says every interactive element has a focus ring.
The "(required)" label text and the Value sample text are not variants; the value text shows as the placeholder color in default and as typed text in the other states.
Helper text is shown in every state. In code it only appears when the helperText prop is set.
Input has no hover state in code or tokens.

components.name: Card

intro.text: A plain container, a link or a button. An interactive card is one control and cannot contain other links or buttons.

whenToUse.text: Kind: static is a plain container. Interactive renders as a link when it has an href, or as a button when it has an onClick.
Use a static card to group related content. Use an interactive card when the whole card is one destination or one choice.
The parts are Card.Header, Card.Title, Card.Body and Card.Footer. Inside an interactive card they render as spans, and the footer is text only.

states.name: default
states.text: The resting card, with the default border.

states.name: hover
states.text: The background changes to the hover color. Interactive cards only.

states.name: pressed
states.text: The background changes to the pressed color. Interactive cards only.

states.name: focus
states.text: A visible 2px focus ring on keyboard focus for every interactive element.

states.name: selected
states.text: A link card marks the current page with aria-current. A button card marks the chosen card with aria-pressed. The border grows to the emphasis width in the accent color.
states.source: Card.tsx, comments on the selected prop

states.name: disabled
states.text: Button cards only. Uses the disabled background and disabled text color for everything inside.

accessibility.text: An interactive card is a single control, so nothing inside it may be interactive. In development the card logs an error if it contains a link or a button.
accessibility.source: Card.tsx, comment above the INTERACTIVE check

accessibility.text: Inside an interactive card the title is a span, not a heading, because links and buttons cannot contain headings.

Interactive cards use a border with a contrast of about 1.4:1, below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks for. This is a recorded decision, with other cues: a surface fill that differs from the page and a focus ring checked at 3:1 or better.
A visible 2px focus ring on keyboard focus for every interactive element, in both themes.

knownGaps: The Figma component has a typed width of 320px. In code the card is as wide as its container and no width token exists.
Static cards only have the default state. The other state combinations are left out of the Figma set (see exclude).
In code the padding shrinks by the border growth when selected, so content does not move. In Figma the stroke is inside the card and does not move content, so padding stays the same.
Link cards and button cards look the same in Figma. Only button cards can be disabled in code.
The title, body and footer text are sample text.
The focus ring is a separate rectangle sized from the variable values, like Button.
Card.tsx has no focus style of its own. The focus ring in Figma follows the README rule.
